title: Bindings workbook: triage and prioritization rubric for enterprise language bindings, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Consolidate incoming enterprise requests for new language client bindings, authentication patterns (SSO/SAML/KMS/token rotation), and streaming ergonomics into a single prioritization workbook and triage rubric. The goal is to produce an actionable roadmap and immediate tactical tickets for Q2 that balance customer urgency, platform effort, and long-term maintainability.

Context: Over the last 9 months we received disparate asks from sales and CSMs for .NET sync clients, Rust zero-copy embeddings, gRPC streaming for high-throughput video annotation pipelines, and SAML SSO patterns for tokenless onboarding. Current intake is fragmented across Zendesk, Salesforce, and ad-hoc PM slack threads which delays consistent evaluation and causes duplicate engineering spikes.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests only (new client libraries, auth patterns, streaming ergonomics). Excludes language bindings where we have an explicit OSS stewarded SDK. This ticket collects requests, defines a scoring rubric, and proposes a first-cut roadmap and immediate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated spreadsheet (workbook) listing all inbound enterprise SDK/client requests with source, customer priority, and minimal technical notes is published to Drive and linked in this ticket.
A triage rubric with weighted scores for customer impact, engineering effort, security/regulatory complexity, and reuse potential is agreed by Eng + Security + Solutions within this cycle.
Top 3 tactical tickets created and scoped with owners (examples: .NET sync client P0 spike, Rust embeddings packaging P1 spike, streaming ergonomics API proposal P1 RFC).
Stakeholder sign-off (Sales lead + SOC/Compliance + two Eng leads) documented in the decision log.
triage_notes: Proposed scoring weights: customer_impact 40%, engineering_effort 25%, security/regulatory 20%, reuse_potential 15% (discussed with Giulia and Liang on 2025-02-20).
Engineering effort buckets: Spike (<2w), Small (2-4w), Medium (1-2mo), Large (>2mo, requires infra changes). Use this to convert score->priority.
Security/regulatory multiplier: any request that touches on on-prem key management or tokenless SSO gets a +15 penalty on effort; require early Security review.
customer_requests_sample: LargeBankCorp: Request a .NET synchronous client with built-in SAML SSO flow and automated token rotation for long-running batch jobs. CSM rated impact as High.
RealTimeDocs: Needs an SSE-based streaming mode (browser-friendly) with reconnect semantics and partial response checkpoints for long-running document annotation sessions. Impact Medium.
GenHealth: Wants an on-prem Python wheel and clear KMS integration pattern for HIPAA workloads; prefers minimal external network calls. Impact High, regulatory flag.
AutoDrive AI: Asks for Rust bindings that can do zero-copy embeddings to avoid allocations in inference loops. Impact Low-Medium but high reuse potential for high-throughput customers.
decision_log: 2025-02-19: Quick alignment — prioritize .NET sync and on-prem Python packaging as top customer-impact items; agreed to treat Rust bindings as a community/OSS-led track unless a named enterprise customer funds it. (Aisha, Marco, Liang)
2025-02-21: Security requested early design review for any tokenless or SAML patterns; added security_review_required flag. (Evelyn)

2025-02-24: Eng owners proposed two spikes: ENG-19077 (.NET auth flow spike) and ENG-19088 (Stream ergonomics RFC + demo). Both spikes estimated as 2wk each; create dependent tickets after workbook finalization. (Liang)
2025-02-25: PM asked Sales to consolidate top-5 paying accounts requesting language bindings and provide renewal risk if not addressed (Jasmine).
next_steps: Finalize Drive workbook with sources column (Zendesk/Salesforce/CSM links) by 2025-02-28 — owner: Marco Santoro.
Kick off security scoping session for SAML/KMS patterns on 2025-03-02 — owner: Evelyn Brooks.
Create and link three tactical Linear tickets for the prioritized spikes by 2025-03-03 (ENG follow-ups).
Publish triage rubric and run one calibration session with Eng + Solutions on 2025-03-04.
